name: Temporal
summary: Temporal runs long, multi-step background work that picks up where it left off after a crash, on Temporal Cloud or on your own servers.

free_plan_covers.note: Temporal Cloud has no lasting free plan: new accounts get $150 in credits that expire after 90 days. The open source server is free to run yourself, but you look after it and its database.

first_paid_usd_month.note: Temporal Cloud has no base monthly fee. You pay for what you use, starting at $50 per million actions plus storage by the hour. Support plans start at $500 a month but are optional.

portability.note: You can move between Temporal Cloud and a server you run yourself without changing code, but your jobs are written as Temporal Workflows and Activities, so leaving Temporal means rewriting them.

sdk_typescript.note: Temporal maintains an official TypeScript SDK (temporalio/sdk-typescript), and @temporalio/create starts a new project.

long_running.note: A Workflow can keep running for years, and if the app crashes Temporal rebuilds its state and carries on where it stopped.

schedules.note: Schedules start a Workflow every set interval or at calendar times like a cron expression, and can be paused, resumed and backfilled.

setup.step: Create a Temporal Cloud account (or run the open source server yourself) and make a Namespace.
Start the project with @temporalio/create to get the TypeScript SDK, a Workflow, an Activity and a Worker.
Put the Namespace's address, its name and an API key in the environment file used by your Worker and client.

builder_notes: Temporal needs a Worker process that stays running to pick up jobs; host it somewhere that runs long-lived processes, not only in serverless functions.
Put network calls and database writes in Activities, not in Workflow code; Workflow code must give the same result every time it is replayed.
Keep TEMPORAL_API_KEY on the server; start Workflows from server code, never from the browser.
